capitals.name: Seiyun (Saywun)
capitals.note: Page: 'with their capital at Seiyun'; the two principal cities were 'Say'un and Tarim'. The page gives no capital dates, so the span is the state's whole life; coordinates are the gazetteer's.

rulers.note: Founder: 'established in 1395 by Badr as-Sahab ibn al-Habrali Bu Tuwairik'; ruled 'until c. 1430'. The page lists no ruler between him and 1865.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The infobox gives no area and no boundary; the Tahirid page says only that the Kathiri 'controlled much of the interior of Hadramawt', and the Kathiri page names Say'un and Tarim as the two principal cities. The disc round Seiyun is the researcher's reading; Shihr is added by the ledger (the 1460s conquest). The lead of the page says 'established in 1379', the history section 1395; 1395 stands.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Qu'aiti 'first took the town of Shibam from the rival Kathiris in 1858' (marked 'citation needed' on the page) and in 1866 'the inland town of Shibam was held by the Qu'aiti tribe', so the 10 km disc round Shibam leaves the shape. The page does not say when, if ever, Shibam returned. The 1937 road from Shihr to Tarim 'runs through the territory of the Kathiri', which fits the wadi shape.

ledger.note: 1395: Badr as-Sahab founds the Kathiri state in the Wadi Hadramawt. 'The Kathiri state was established in 1395 by Badr as-Sahab ibn al-Habrali Bu Tuwairik' (the lead says 1379); the capital was at Seiyun. The page gives no territory; the region is the researcher's reading and the Rasulid page does not show that the land had a state before.

region.text: Shihr in Hadramawt, the port and district

ledger.note: 1460s: the Kathiri conquer Shihr. 'The Kathiri conquered Ash-Shihr in the 1460s.' The Tahirid page has Shihr taken by the Tahirids in 1457 and 'lost at the end of the fifteenth century' to 'the Kathiri princedom that controlled much of the interior of Hadramawt', and the Tahirid dossier records the loss in 1499 (confidence 1); the two pages disagree and the Kathiri page's decade is rounded to 1465 here.

region.text: the town of Shibam, taken by the Qu'aiti in 1858 and held by them in 1866

ledger.note: 1858: the Qu'aiti take Shibam. 'the sons of Umar bin Awadh al-Qu'aiti first took the town of Shibam from the rival Kathiris in 1858' (the page marks the sentence 'citation needed'); in 1866 'the inland town of Shibam was held by the Qu'aiti tribe'.

region.text: Shihr in Hadramawt, the port and district

ledger.note: 1866: the Kathiri sultan retakes the fort at Shihr. 'In 1866, Sultan Ghalib bin Muhsin, Sheikh of the Kathiri, expelled Ali bin Naji from Shihr and took possession of the fort.' The page implies Shihr was in other hands before; no page opened dates when the Kathiri lost it after the 1460s, so the dossier keeps it Kathiri from 1465 and this event moves no land.

region.text: Shihr in Hadramawt, the port and district

ledger.note: 1867: the Qu'aiti take Shihr. 'In April 1867, Awadh bin Umar landed near Shihr' and 'established the authority of his brother as Jemadar of Shihr'; in December 1867 the Kathiri tried to retake it and were 'repulsed by the Qu'aiti, who have since remained in unmolested possession of the port and district.' The month is the landing; the page does not say when the Kathiri garrison left.

region.text: 'the port at Dhufar', read as Salalah, the port of Dhofar

ledger.note: 1895: the Kathiri seize the port of Dhofar. 'In 1895, the Kathiri captured the port at Dhufar, driving out the Governor.' The page does not say whose governor; the counterpart is the researcher's reading (the page says elsewhere that the Kathiri 'lost its eastern regions to the Omani Empire and the Mahra Sultanate'). Salalah is read from 'the port at Dhufar'.

region.text: 'the port at Dhufar', read as Salalah, the port of Dhofar

ledger.note: 1897: the port is lost again. 'In 1897 the port was recaptured.' The page does not name the recapturing power.

ledger.note: 1967, November: the Kathiri state ends in South Yemen. 'Al-Husayn ibn Ali, Kathiri sultan since 1949, was overthrown in October 1967. The following month the former sultanate became part of newly independent South Yemen.'

wars.name: Kathiri-Qu'aiti struggle for Shibam and Shihr

Shihr in Hadramawt, the port and district

wars.outcome: The Qu'aiti took Shibam in 1858 and Shihr in 1867 and 'have since remained in unmolested possession of the port and district'; 'In 1918, a long standing Qu'aiti-Kathiri quarrel was settled' (Kathiri page; its terms are not given).
wars.note: 1866: the Kathiri sultan took the fort at Shihr from Ali bin Naji; April 1867: the Qu'aiti landed; December 1867: the Kathiri attack on Shihr was repulsed. The British declined to intervene in the 1866-1867 disputes. The fighting is dated 1858 and 1866-1867 only; 1918 is the settlement.

wars.name: Kathiri seizure of the port of Dhofar

zones.text: 'the port at Dhufar', read as Salalah, the port of Dhofar

wars.outcome: The Kathiri captured the port in 1895 'driving out the Governor'; 'In 1897 the port was recaptured'.
wars.note: The same page records an earlier plan: 'In 1414, Sultan Ali bin Omar bin Jaafar bin Badr al-Kathiri decided to seize Dhofar', without saying what came of it. The belligerent 'sultanate-of-oman' is the researcher's reading of 'the Governor'.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary of the Kathiri lands, only towns (Seiyun, Tarim, Shibam, Shihr); the British protection (advisory treaties of the 1940s and 1950s, the Eastern Protectorate from 1940) fixed no Kathiri frontier on the pages opened.

notes: No Cliopatria row. The Kathiri have no extent on any page opened (infobox: no area; Tahirid page: 'much of the interior of Hadramawt'), so the shape is a 120 km disc round Seiyun, soft, and a gap-filler with a map source should replace it. Disagreements: (1) Shihr: the Kathiri page has the conquest in the 1460s, the Tahirid page and the Tahirid dossier (ledger 5, confidence 1) put the loss at the end of the 15th century (1499); this dossier takes 1465 and the Tahirid dossier's later date finds no land to move. (2) Founding: the lead says 1379, the history 1395. (3) The last sultan: the table says al-Muhsin bin Ali (1948-1967), the text Al-Husayn ibn Ali (sultan since 1949). Silences: how the Kathiri held Shihr between the 1460s and 1866 (the 1866 sentence implies other hands); when the 'eastern regions' went to the Omani Empire and the Mahra Sultanate (undated); what became of the 1414 plan to seize Dhofar; the terms of the 1918 Qu'aiti-Kathiri settlement; the year of the British protection treaty (the infobox lists one, the extraction shows no year; the Aden Protectorate page names the Kathiri only among the Eastern Protectorate states with advisory treaties of the 1940s and 1950s). The Kathiri page also says 'In the mid-1950s, the Kathiri state was forced to join the British Protectorate of South Arabia' (the Aden Protectorate page dates that protectorate to 18 January 1963); the protectorate relation is the Aden Protectorate and United Kingdom dossiers' to carry, so no vassal event is written here. The Aden Protectorate dossier (1886-1967) and this one may draw the same wadi. Needs dossiers from another group: the Qu'aiti State of Shihr and Mukalla (1858-1967, slug qu-aiti-state-of-shihr-and-mukalla), counterpart of the 1858 and 1867 losses; until it exists the Shibam and Shihr discs fall to nobody's land. Gazetteer: places Saywun, Shibam, Ash Shihr, Salalah resolve; 'Tarim' (Yemen) has no place entry (the gazetteer has only the Tarim Basin), so Tarim is covered by the disc round Seiyun and needs adding as a place.
